content.text: {"relation":"REFINED","consensus_summary":"Light broadly signifies God’s holy, life-giving presence and truth, especially as revealed in Christ, with recognized derivative senses including God’s law, moral righteousness, and believers’ visible witness through good works.","book_summary":"Light is God’s law embodied in publicly visible righteous conduct—good works that others can see.","consensus_core_identification":"Divine holiness, truth, and life made manifest, including derivatively righteous guidance and witness.","book_core_identification":"Divine law visibly enacted as good works.","core_relation":"BOOK_NARROWS","extension_relation":"BOOK_SUBSET","boundary_disagreement":"The book restricts light to the intersection of two accepted applications—law and believers’ visible good works—thereby excluding or leaving aside the broader consensus cases in which light directly denotes God, Christ, revelation, salvation, life, or glory.","material_contradiction":"There is no necessary contradiction in the cited contexts because both law-as-light and visible righteous witness are recognized consensus senses. The disagreement arises only if the entry is intended as an exhaustive definition of light across Scripture.","rationale":"The book does not introduce an unknown referent or replace the consensus with an incompatible one. Proverbs 6:23 explicitly associates law with light, while Matthew 5:16 links shining light with publicly seen good works. The book synthesizes these established strands into a materially narrower identification rather than preserving the full polyvalent consensus.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"The two citations support law as light and good works as visible light separately, but they do not conclusively establish that every biblical use of light means law embodied in works; major passages directly identify light with God or Christ.","confidence":"high"}
